# Using this wiki

Anyone can read the wiki. Editing happens right on the page, and every change is kept as a draft in your browser until you save, so you can try things freely. Saving publishes to the repo and needs a GitHub token with write access.

## Two kinds of pages

Most pages are **documents**, like this one: a single column of blocks you read from top to bottom, much like Notion or Obsidian. A few are **canvases**, free boards where cards sit wherever you put them, closer to OneNote. Canvases suit diagrams and one screen summaries like the [[io-cheatsheet]], documents suit everything else. The page settings switch a page between the two.

## Writing in a document

Press **Edit** in the toolbar, or E. The page looks exactly the same, but you can now click into any text and type. Formatting happens as you write, using the shortcuts Markdown uses:

| Type | To get |
| --- | --- |
| `#`, `##` or `###` and a space | A heading |
| `-` and a space | A bulleted list |
| `1.` and a space | A numbered list |
| `[]` and a space | A to-do item |
| `>` and a space | A quote |
| `---` and a space | A divider |
| `` ``` `` and a space | A code block |
| `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, `~~struck~~` | Formatting, applied when you type the closing marker |
| `[[` | A link to another page, picked from a list |

Type `/` at the start of a line, or after a space, to open the block menu with headings, lists, callouts, code, tables, images, video and drawings. Selecting text shows a small toolbar with bold, italic, links and headings, and Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+E for code and Ctrl+K for a link work as well. Enter on an empty line at the end of a quote or callout steps back out of it.

Hover a block to see its handle on the left. Drag the handle to move the block. Click it for a menu to duplicate or delete the block, hide it from the published page, or edit its Markdown source directly. The + beside the handle inserts a new block below.

## Arranging a canvas

On a canvas, right click empty space or press Shift+A to add a card where you point. Drag a card to move it and drag its edges to resize it. Double click a text, code or table card to edit it, with the same formatting as in a document. Scroll to pan, Ctrl+scroll or pinch to zoom, and use the buttons in the corner to fit everything on screen.

## Links, search and callouts

A link written as `[[slug]]` points at another page by its slug or title, and `[[slug|other words]]` changes the text that is shown. A link to a page that does not exist yet is drawn dashed. At the bottom of every document you can see which pages link to it.

Press Ctrl+K anywhere outside a text block, or click the search field in the sidebar, to search every page by title and text.

Callouts are for things a reader must not miss. In Markdown they are quotes whose first line names the kind, with an optional title after it:

cards.code:
> [!WARNING] Optional title
> The text of the callout.

cards.md: NOTE, TIP, WARNING, DANGER and EXAMPLE are available, and the block menu inserts the first three. Each has its own icon and label as well as its colour, so they read the same whichever colours you can tell apart.

## Saving

Edits stay drafts until you press **Save**. Drafts live in this browser only, so they survive a reload but do not follow you to another device. A dot on the Save button, and next to a page in the sidebar, shows what is not published yet.

**Save** publishes every page with unsaved changes in a single commit. The first time, it asks for a fine grained GitHub token with *Contents: Read and write* on Paraxdev/GodotTrench. The token stays in this browser's storage and is only ever sent to api.github.com. GitHub Pages then needs a minute or so to redeploy, and until it has, the wiki keeps showing your saved version from the browser.

Outside a text block, Ctrl+Z undoes changes to the page, such as a deleted or moved block, and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes them. Inside a text block they undo and redo your typing as usual.

If a page changed in the repo while you had a draft of it, for example because you edited it on another device, the page shows a banner that lets you keep your draft or take the repo version. **Refresh** in the sidebar throws away every draft and reloads everything from the repo.

## Images and media

Paste an image straight into a document or onto a canvas, or use the upload button on an image block. With a token set, the file is committed to `wiki/assets` and the page links to it. Without one it is embedded in the page itself, which works but makes the page file large. Image blocks take a caption, and video blocks take an mp4 link or a YouTube or Vimeo address.
